L25n438.description: A digit in the middle of a number or counting sequence (the 3 in 0,1,2,3; the 0 in 80,000; the 1 in 4,100); pushes toward closing quote and punctuation tokens.

L26n3006.name: Mid-word fragment, magic
L26n3006.description: The inner pieces of words split into several tokens (omn|isc|ient, Iris german|ica, Jun|...); pushes 'magic', 'spell' and 'enchanted'.

L25n1518.name: Name-internal subword pieces
L25n1518.description: Fires (negative) on a non-initial subword piece of a multi-token proper name, strongest on 'ob' in Chern|ob|yl and 'qu' in Tar|qu|inius, mostly in place names, people and titles. Pushes toward 'parameter' and 'parameters'; steering shows no clear effect.

L26n1212.name: Digit before thousands comma
L26n1212.description: Fires on the digit right before a thousands comma in a large number (the 0 in 10,000 or 3,000, the 2 in 12,000), weaker on other digits of numbers above a thousand. Pushes toward ',' and pushed hard it spams commas.

L26n800.name: Opening quote or parenthesis
L26n800.description: Goes negative on an opening quote, dash or parenthesis that starts an aside or a defined term (“tear film”, — don't use, (minimum inhibitory); pushes '('.

L26n2957.name: List separator comma
L26n2957.description: Goes negative on the comma or 'and' between items in a noun list (wild turkeys, alligators; peas, beans); pushes 'capacity'.

L25n2480.name: Preposition before recipient
L25n2480.description: The function word right before the recipient or object of a verb in feature descriptions (allows [users], enables, for diners, to everyday objects); pushes 'end'.

L26n375.name: Connector before its object
L26n375.description: Fires (negative) on the preposition or conjunction that introduces an object or list item: 'by' in ravaged by fire, 'against' in protection against, 'like' in like a cold, 'or' in seizures or, plus the comma in lists such as ulcers, cracked tooth. Pushes toward 'circular' and 'adaptive' adjectives; pushed, it spams 'circular'.

L26n1800.name: Prefix stubs: nan, con
L26n1800.description: Fires (negative) on the short first piece of a scientific or long word split into tokens: 'nan' in nanoscale and nanomedicine, 'Ag' in Ag@SiO2, 'con' in conquering and coniferous, 'an' in nanosecond, 'cur' in curtailed. Pushes toward '@' and 'norm'-style tokens; steering has no clear effect.

L26n1990.name: Word-stub starts (c, cur)
L26n1990.description: Fires (negative) on a one- or two-letter stub that begins an ordinary word split into tokens, e.g. 'c' in ceded, 'cur' in curtailed, 'ch' in chops, 'sn' in snags, and capital stubs like 'Ch' in Chalmette. Pushes toward 'cut' and 'cutting'; pushed, it spams 'cut'.

L26n1902.name: Start of split names
L26n1902.description: The first or second piece of a split name or word (Mos|he, Rom|mel, mol|ars, ul|cers, Si Thammarat); pushes 'keep'.

L26n1420.name: Mixed subword fragments
L26n1420.description: Diffuse: fires on odd word-internal pieces and lone letters in split words (Ophi|og|lossaceae, Wollong|ong, neur|al, the g in sweet|gums), and on 'for' before a data or software object ('Core Data for data persistence'). Pushes toward 'data'; pushed, it spams 'data'.

L25n91.name: URL starts, closing terms
L25n91.description: Diffuse: fires (negative) on 'http' or 'https' starting a URL (://), and on the word just before a closing bracket or quote, e.g. '<package-name>', 'learning rate', 'may be present'. Pushes toward quote and closing characters; steering gives no clear effect.

L25n1981.name: Stem before -ed suffix
L25n1981.description: Fires on the stem piece of a verb split from its past-tense ending, just before '-ed', '-ied' or '-ified' (well-m|aint|ained, reb|uk|ed, priv|atis|ed, Otherwise Spec|ified). Pushes toward 'd' and 'ed' endings; pushed, it spams 'dd' and 'red'.

L26n3000.name: Name-start pieces (New, Z)
L26n3000.description: Fires (negative) on the first token of a capitalised name split into pieces, before the completing piece: 'New' in New Year's and New Jersey, 'Maz' in Mazaheri, 'Z' in Zephaniah and Zheng, 'Re' in Reformation, 'Tong' in Tonga. Pushes toward 'xml'; steering shows no clear effect.

L25n2793.name: Modal before a verb
L25n2793.description: Goes negative on a modal, auxiliary or 'to' right after a subject, before a main verb (would, will, was, were, to, which); pushes 'take', 'carry' and 'bring'.

L25n2931.name: Modifier before 'history'
L25n2931.description: Fires (negative) on the modifier just before a head noun, strongest on 'family' in family history and 'browsing' in browsing history, plus 'medical' before provider and 'a' before stroke or disability. Pushes toward 'history' and 'historical'; pushed, it spams 'historian'.

L26n2038.name: Word-start al/sh pieces
L26n2038.description: Word-start 'al' or 'sh' pieces (Alka|Seltzer, al|bacore, sh|aver, Sh|ippuden); pushes plural nouns such as 'genes', 'words' and 'items'.

L26n293.name: Math and code symbols
L26n293.description: Fires (negative) on symbols inside formulas, code and abbreviations: hex digits in 0x82, the ∂ in ∂A, the o in ApoE, the comma between function arguments (t, y), and the dot in F.D.R. or M.D. Pushes toward uppercase code-like tokens such as AA, MA and IME; steering gives no clear effect.

L26n2979.name: HTML tag brackets (canvas)
L26n2979.description: Fires (negative) on the angle brackets and tag name of HTML tags, strongest on the > that ends <canvas> and on the word canvas itself; weaker on random word stubs such as hem, Kr and Ne. Pushes toward 'tag' and 'Element'; pushed, it spams 'tag tag'.

L25n1422.name: Proper-noun first piece
L25n1422.description: The first piece of a capitalized name (Saint|Francis, Van|Gogh, Car|cassonne, Col|enso, Rep. Maloney); pushes 'origin' and 'start'.

L26n2865.name: Split name stems
L26n2865.description: Fires on the first piece of a split capitalized name or word (Ser-enity, Sar-abhai, Sk-opje, Br-eathing, Dal-ālat), right before its continuation; pushes 'le' tokens, and pushed output spams 'Le le le'.

L26n646.name: Person names, pushes John
L26n646.description: Strongly negative on given names and surnames of people (Alonzo, Leland, Ulysses, Catherine, Brian Crossley), most on the name token itself; pushes 'John' and common male-name tokens.

L25n1258.name: Latin word-start stems
L25n1258.description: Strongly negative on the first sub-token of a Latin genus, plant or rare name split into pieces (Ar-buscular, Ar-bequina, Cr-ataegus, c-arambola, Ar-nett); pushes 'optional' tokens.

L25n1544.name: Modifier before function
L25n1544.description: Fires on the word just before 'function', 'purpose' or 'task' (primary, different, same, their, this, many, whose, biological), in sentences about what something does; pushes 'function' tokens.

L26n2533.name: Word-initial N fragments
L26n2533.description: Fires on a word-initial 'N' or 'n' fragment, usually a capitalized or split word start (N-ell, N-imetz, N-esting, n-ose, N-ausea, Gran-ada, C-en-ozoic); pushes 'zero', 'null' and 'NaN' tokens.

L26n314.name: Apostrophe and prime fragments
L26n314.description: Diffuse: fires on the letter or digit just before an apostrophe or prime (l in l'Heure, d in d'état, 3 in 3′-UTR, x in x′, 0 in 8.0); pushes curly apostrophes and closing quotes.

L26n944.name: Capitalized name starts
L26n944.description: Fires on the first sub-token of a capitalized name or split technical word (L-oyalists, L-ifespan, Al-fonso, Dyn in DNS provider Dyn, poly-gamy, poly-ethylene); pushes 'money', 'data' and 'information'.

L25n1853.name: Word before space nouns
L25n1853.description: Fires on the modifier right before a place noun such as space, area, zone or quarters (living quarters, enclosed spaces, safe space, storage areas, nuclear wasteland); pushes 'area', 'region' and 'zone'.

L26n2714.name: V/fe word starts
L26n2714.description: Fires on a short 'v' or 'fe'/'ev'/'av' sub-token starting a word fragment (vibrate, vaccinated, vaping, fevers, evaporation, Avot, lemons); pushes 'want' and 'desired' tokens.

L25n617.name: Mature and place-name subjects
L25n617.description: Fires on the word 'mature' (mature seeds, mature eggs, mature forests, mature audience) and on country or city subjects after 'has/does/was' (Singapore, Chilean); pushes stray single-letter tokens (n, h, i, k).

L25n1523.name: Adverbs before main verb
L25n1523.description: Diffuse: fires on an adverb or 'to' that sits between an auxiliary and its main verb (have also suggested, were also found, only formally recognized, clearly entitles), plus the name Alonzo; pushes 'point' and 'points'.

L26n1805.name: Word starts and the
L26n1805.description: Fires on the first sub-token of a split word (dist-illery, inst-igated, Bo-aters, Dev-onta) and on 'the' before a team or organization name (the Denver Nuggets, the New York Giants); pushes 'primary' and 'secondary'.

L26n2804.name: Rare-word start fragments
L26n2804.description: Fires on the first sub-token of a rare or split word (Bur-j Khalifa, Bur-ial, sil-houettes, lif-eguards, acc-io in carpaccio, incub-ation, ilit-ers); pushes 'io' and 'os' suffix tokens.

L25n1099.name: Re- prefix starts
L25n1099.description: Fires on the 're' sub-token that opens a prefixed word (re-assemble, re-expands, re-processing, reconfigurable, re-signed, reappeared); pushes 'feedback' tokens.

L26n334.name: Digits in numeric values
L26n334.description: Fires on a digit token inside a number or date (the 6 in 60.1 °F, 8 in Mar. 8, the 0 in 1.0, 2 in 826V) and on name fragments (Ast-, Ab-, Ikh-); pushes 'six' and '6' tokens.

L25n17.name: Un- and re- prefixes
L25n17.description: Fires on the 'un' or 're' prefix that starts a word (unclaimed, unaccompanied, unregulated, unifier, re-appeared, relearned) and on 'under' in under-delivery; pushes 'another', 'again' and 'multiple'.

L26n2689.name: Em/om word starts
L26n2689.description: Negative on a short 'em', 'om' or 'Prom' fragment starting a word split by the tokenizer (em-itter, high-em-ission, om-itted, Prom-ising, rem-olded); pushes the 'itt', 'ited' and 'itter' completions.

L25n556.name: Digits in dates/refs
L25n556.description: Fires on the digit or separator inside a date, verse or figure number (the 1 in January 1, 1863; the colon in Mark 9:11; 5.11 in Figure 5.11; the 1 in ICD-10); pushes stray 'l' tokens.

L26n850.name: Technical word fragments
L26n850.description: Fires on a mid-word sub-token of a long technical, Greek or Latin word (Pol-yst-yrene, som-atostatin, Ophi-ost-oma, ep-igenetic, mult-iloc-ular, asth-ma); pushes '{' and '[' brackets.

L25n1623.name: Titles and historical adjectives
L25n1623.description: Diffuse: fires on adjectives and title words in citations and descriptions (exact, Historical, Harper, Hist-ories, Ant, Print); pushes 're' and 'heavy' tokens.

L26n1109.name: 'ho' fragment and names
L26n1109.description: Fires on the 'ho' piece of words split into tokens (hoarding, Hooves, Leeuwenhoek) and on the first piece of some surnames; pushes the model toward 'Chinese' and 'China', so steered output becomes 'Chinese' spam.

L26n585.name: Mid-word fragments, 'across'
L26n585.description: Fires on a word-piece in the middle of a split word or name (oul in Boulton, ile in acoustic neuroma, rel in relatable, par in paralyze); pushes toward 'across', 'between', 'along', so steered output spams 'across'.

L25n1307.name: Retail store nouns
L25n1307.description: Goes strongly negative on the store-type noun in shopping text ('store' in grocery store, 'retail', 'supermarket', 'online stores', 'mall'); pushing it negative makes the model spam 'store'.

L26n966.name: Sound and hearing context
L26n966.description: Goes strongly negative on the comma or word just before a sound sense in sensory lists ('sight, sound', 'smell, taste') and on 'sc' in screech; pushing it negative makes the model spam 'listen' and 'hear'.

L26n2527.name: Stem-cell differentiation, 'self'
L26n2527.description: Fires on words in stem-cell and differentiation text, peaking on the 'and' or 'into' just before a differentiation or cell-fate term ('integration and differentiation', 'differentiated into'); pushes toward 'self', so steered output spams 'self'.

L25n776.name: First letter of names
L25n776.description: Goes strongly negative on the single first letter of a capitalised name (U in Utrecht, R in Rama, l in limes); pushes toward closing quote marks, with no clear steered effect.

L26n2819.name: Word-start fragments (Ber)
L26n2819.description: Goes strongly negative on the first 1-3 letters of a word split into pieces, usually a capitalised name or term (Ber in Berzelius, Ver in Verilog, H in Hittite); pushes toward code markers 'TODO' and 'FIXME', with little steered effect.

L25n929.name: 'Ar' word-start fragments
L25n929.description: Goes strongly negative on 'Ar' or 'ar' opening a word fragment (arbuscules, Arnett, Archonditsis, armpits); pushes toward 'possess', 'having', 'belongs', so steered output reads 'possess having belonged'.

L26n1754.name: Mid-word subword fragments
L26n1754.description: Goes strongly negative on a middle piece of a long word split into tokens (hou in Mabhouh, act in monobactams, apt in Diphyllobothrium, roph in neutrophils); pushes toward 'rem' and 'em' fragments, so steered output becomes 'remembrance' spam.

L26n196.name: Mid-word fragment, noisy output
L26n196.description: Fires on the middle piece of a split word (ien in experienced, ys in cryptanalysing, iv in Conceivably, poss in possessor) and on the digit '1' in 1611; pushes toward unrelated fragments like 'FX' and 'lx' with no clear steered effect.

L25n1745.name: Pest and pet words
L25n1745.description: Goes strongly negative on 'pest' in Yersinia pestis and pest control, and on pet, outdoor and flea words in animal-care and disease text; pushes toward 'space' and 'room', so steered output spams 'room'.

L25n109.name: Month names and pairs
L25n109.description: Fires on month names in dates (August, December, June) and on 'vs', 'between' and 'and' joining two values; pushes toward 'against', so steered output spams 'against'.

L25n1339.name: Name-start word fragments
L25n1339.description: Fires on the first piece of a split name or word (Mon in Monopoly and Monrovia, Lever in Leverkusen, Str in Stroudwater, Tim in Tim Burton); pushes toward 'against', 'contra' and 'resistance', so steered output spams 'against'.

L26n1051.name: 'Im' word-starts
L26n1051.description: Goes strongly negative on 'Im' or 'imm' word-starts (Immaculate, Immune, immemorial) and on nouns like card, tea, oil and image; pushes toward 'test', so steered output spams 'test'.

L26n2084.name: Electricity and voltage words
L26n2084.description: Fires on electrical-domain words, peaking on 'electrical', 'electric' and 'welding', and on 'high' or 'low' before 'voltage'; pushes toward 'current' and 'resistance', so steered output spams 'current'.

L26n1789.name: Mid-word name fragments
L26n1789.description: Fires on the second or third piece of a multi-token name or word (har in Philharmonic, adel in Philadelphus, chie in mischievous, osl in Yaroslavl); pushes toward 'f' fragments like 'fine' and 'fe', so steered output becomes word-piece noise.

L26n302.name: Closing punctuation before breaks
L26n302.description: Fires on punctuation that closes a unit: a colon or newline before a quoted or listed item, a closing quote after '?' or '.', and a bar or closing bracket at a label boundary; pushes toward closing quote marks, with little visible steered effect.

L26n263.name: Opening parenthesis before aside
L26n263.description: Fires on an opening '(' right after a title, code, unit or number ('Edexcel GCSE (9-1)', 'Figure 5.11 (d)', '64.0°F (17.8°C)'); pushes toward word-ending fragments like 'rk', 'rn', 'rd', with no clear steered effect.

L25n2099.name: Word-start 'ther/Her' fragments
L25n2099.description: Fires on the first piece of a split word (ther in thermostatic, ter in termites, Her in Herat, Tra in Trauma, Archae in Archaeological); pushes toward 'traditional' and 'conventional', so steered output spams 'Traditional'.

L25n2196.name: Word before 'way/path'
L25n2196.description: Fires on the word right before a route noun: 'this' in 'this way', 'along' in 'along the way', 'career' in 'career path', 'sure' in 'sure way'; pushes the model toward 'path', so steered output spams 'path'.

L26n45.name: Named-example introducer words
L26n45.description: Fires on the word right before a named example or entity list ('such *as* Amazon', 'sites *like* Napster', 'including the Air Force'), mostly brand and agency names. Pushes toward hardware and tech proper nouns (FPGA, VGA, SCSI).

L26n1293.name: Split 'v'/'dev' fragments
L26n1293.description: Fires on short fragment tokens 'v', 'dev', 'div' inside split words (V|ORTEX, Dev|iance, di|v|estment, -v|accinated). Mid-word pieces, not whole words. Pushes toward 'var', 'variant' and 'variation' completions.

L25n2905.name: Predicts 'best' after 'our'
L25n2905.description: Fires on 'our' in 'do our part' and on mid-word fragments of split names and words (A|by|ei, S|eps|is, Hojib|lan|ca). Pushes toward 'best', plus 'optimal' and 'recommended'.

L26n1812.name: '-ary' word-stem fragments
L26n1812.description: Fires on the stem fragment just before a '-ary', '-arian' or '-itated' ending (sanct|u|aries, benefici|aries, veterin|arians, pituit|ary). Pushes toward 'ar' starts like 'arm' and 'arc'.

L25n1019.name: Goal verbs; 'options' output
L25n1019.description: Fires on the verb right after a subject in a how-to or goal sentence ('can *avoid* mistakes', 'Leaders must *ensure*', 'reduces', 'provide', 'identify'). Pushes toward 'options' tokens.

L25n1700.name: Capital name-starts; '[' output
L25n1700.description: Fires on the first capital letter or abbreviation start of a proper name or code term (E in E.coli, C in C++, Fort in Fort Stanwix). Also fires on 'https' and 'chars' in URLs and code. Pushes toward an opening square bracket '['.

L25n318.name: Name-fragment letters; ';' output
L25n318.description: Fires on a capital letter or short abbreviation piece inside a name or code label (ApoE, the '-N' of PDD-NOS, De|indl, Di|aptomus, C chains). Pushes toward semicolon tokens.

L26n472.name: Math and table operators
L26n472.description: Fires on operator and punctuation tokens between numbers or inside equations, code and tables ('=', '×', ':', ',', '|', '→'). Pushes toward ligature and ellipsis tokens ('ﬁ', 'ﬂ', '...').

L26n120.name: Code identifiers, not prose
L26n120.description: Fires on arrows, dashes and file-extension tokens in code and command lines ('->', 'sh', '.py', 'HTML', 'AWS'). Pushes toward programming type and class names (DataFrame, Headers, MyClass, UIImage).

L25n648.name: Di-/Br- starts; 'different' output
L25n648.description: Fires on the first fragment of words starting Di, Dis, Br or nond- (nond|iscriminatory, Di|wali, Br|unsbüttel, Dis|secting). Pushes toward 'different', 'distinct' and 'differ'.

L25n2994.name: Words before 'market'
L25n2994.description: Fires on the noun or fragment just before 'market' (job, soft drinks, target audience) and on 'yc' in sycamore. Pushes toward 'market' and 'markets'.

L25n2998.name: Dollar sign and prompt
L25n2998.description: Fires on '$' before dollar amounts ($230,000, $15 minimum wage) and on the '~' and ']$' of shell prompts. Pushes toward '$'-prefixed tokens like $d, $q and $x.

L26n1679.name: Before data-structure nouns
L26n1679.description: Fires on the modifier before a data-structure or technical noun (sorted array, singly linked list, splay tree data structure). Pushes toward 'map' and 'Map'.

L25n1110.name: Physical motion; 'left/front' output
L25n1110.description: Fires on a physical movement or posture word after 'like', 'between' or 'brakes,' (crawling, upright, kicked, motorcycle). Pushes toward spatial direction words 'left' and 'front'.

L26n560.name: Compound-noun modifiers; 'E' output
L26n560.description: Fires on the modifier word that starts a compound noun or fixed phrase (tummy in tummy time, scrambled in scrambled egg, problem in problem-solving, meat in meat-eaters). Pushes toward bare 'E' token repetition.

L26n2351.name: 'helpful' in assistant prompts
L26n2351.description: Fires on 'helpful' in 'You are a helpful assistant' system prompts and on 'help' in help desk. Pushes toward 'main' and 'character' tokens.

L25n2651.name: Building-part noun fragments
L25n2651.description: Fires on the first piece of a physical structure noun in construction or object text (j|amb, t|urret, m|ounds, tread|mill, bons|ai). Pushes toward 'plate', 'platform' and 'board'.

L26n593.name: Dot-letter abbreviations; '.c' output
L26n593.description: Fires on the period and letter inside abbreviations or initials (p.m., a.d., U.S., E.P., M.P.H.) and on diacritic name letters. Pushes toward file-extension tokens '.c', '.h', '.cpp' and '.java'.

L26n817.name: Word fragments before 'benefit'
L26n817.description: Fires on the word-start fragment before a rare or multi-token word (Cor|rimal, vag|rancy, Mont|adale, clus|al) and on 'it' in 'how it can'. Pushes toward 'benefit' and 'benefits'.

L26n2472.name: Proper-name starts; '.' output
L26n2472.description: Fires on the first letter or fragment of a capitalized name (Bel|nap, Fl|ora, Pal|umbo, Pr|ima). Pushes toward period and dot-like punctuation ('.', '/.').

L25n409.name: Mojibake reads, code closers
L25n409.description: Reads mojibake and accented-letter fragments in garbled text; pushes toward closing quotes and parentheses.

L26n1940.name: Stems before past participles
L26n1940.description: The stem piece of a verb just before its past-participle ending, such as 'ble' in bleached, 'dw' in dwelt, 'heart' in heartbroken, and 'explo' in unexplored. Pushes toward past participles like 'taken', 'written', 'gone'.

L26n162.name: Lead-ins before examples
L26n162.description: The token right before an explanation or example list: an opening '(' before an abbreviation, a ':' before a list, 'eg' before examples, 'for' before a value. Pushes toward 'description', 'report', 'observation'.

L25n2232.name: Ordinal sequence words
L25n2232.description: Sequence words that mark a stage of something, such as 'next', 'second', 'first', 'previous' in 'the next phase' or 'the second wave'. Pushes toward 'round', 'Round', 'rounds'.

L26n2320.name: Word-start 'Rep' fragments
L26n2320.description: The first piece of a split word, mostly 'Rep' or 'rep' (Repat, Representative, repurpose), also 'Commod' and 'Nem'. Pushes toward 'position' and 'positions'.

L25n2133.name: Food and customer nouns
L25n2133.description: Food, shopping and customer nouns such as pizza, supermarket, lunch, beer, coffee, cake, customer, firing on the noun and the word right after the lead-in. Pushes toward 'order' and 'orders'.

L25n2240.name: Stems before '-ia' endings
L25n2240.description: The middle piece of a long technical or literary word just before its '-ia' ending, such as 'hythm' in arrhythmia, 'leg' in tetraplegia, 'lex' in dyslexia, 'alg' in nostalgia. Pushes toward 'ia', 'ie', 'ías'.

L25n1854.name: Books and fiction words
L25n1854.description: Book and literature words such as novels, fiction, fantasy, thriller, literary, books, and 'to' before read or use in reviews. Pushes toward 'read' and 'reading'.

L26n1066.name: Split proper-name openers
L26n1066.description: The first piece of a capitalized name or noun split into tokens, such as 'Lu' in Lucretia, 'Ju' in juice, 'Cr' in Crataegus, 'Kr' in Krusty. Pushes toward 'http', 'https', 'www'.

L26n3056.name: Split proper-name middles
L26n3056.description: The middle piece of a capitalized name split into tokens, such as 'ib' in Dibrell, 'Sk' in Skopje, 'Mer' in Merck, 'Sch' in Schuman. Pushes toward 'course' and 'courses'.

L26n1589.name: 'self' compound prefix
L26n1589.description: 'self' as the first half of a compound such as self-esteem, self-defense, self-raising, self-sufficiency, self-concepts. Pushes toward blank placeholders like '__'.

L26n1058.name: Verb-phrase filler slots
L26n1058.description: A filler word inside a verb phrase, such as 'a' in 'give e-cigarettes a go', 'it' in 'I thought it', 'you' in 'get you writing', plus random word-start fragments like 'Har' and 'wh'. Pushes toward 'bit' and 'bits'.

L25n1091.name: Computer and screen words
L25n1091.description: Computer and device words such as tablet, screen, display, laptop, desktop, smart home, monitor. Pushes toward 'PC', 'computer', 'monitor' and 'Mac'.

L26n232.name: Genomics and science terms
L26n232.description: Molecular and lab-science terms such as genome, genomic, transcript, sequencing, polymer, fracture, glycosylated, plus 'Un' in 'unidentified'. Pushes toward '[' and '[[' bracket tokens.

L26n376.name: Capitalized name openers
L26n376.description: The first one or two letters of a capitalized name split into pieces, such as 'Gra' in Graubünden, 'Fra' in Fraunhofer, 'Ja' in Jaipur, 'Zu' in Zigetsu. Pushes toward word endings 'n', 'ities', 'ians'.

L25n1090.name: Digits and kana mid-token
L25n1090.description: Mid-token pieces inside numbers and Japanese verbs: the middle digit of a temperature or year (18|6|9) and kana verb endings (た, い, を). Pushes toward '。' and ')'.

L26n1676.name: Prefixed word stems, medical
L26n1676.description: The stem piece before a word's second half in prefixed or compound words, such as 'heart' in heartbreak, 'post' in post-breakup, 'asy' in parasympathetic, 'phys' in physiotherapy. Pushes toward 'operation' and 'operations'.

L25n3034.name: Last digit before degrees
L25n3034.description: The last digit of a number right before a degree unit, such as the 5 in '35 °C' or '40 degrees F', and the words Celsius and Fahrenheit. Pushes toward 'degree' and 'degrees'.

L26n1654.name: Proper-name stems, 'data'
L26n1654.description: The first piece of a split proper noun or period name, such as 'Mi' in Miocene, 'Ne' in Neolithic, 'Hel' in Heliodorus, 'Mel'. Pushes toward 'data', '_data', 'Data'.

L25n855.name: Technical terms, 'change'
L25n855.description: Mixed technical terms: 'Hor' (Horowitz, Horrible), 'py' in enthalpy, 'Therm', 'Pro', plus 'of' or 'average' in definitions like 'rate of change'. Pushes toward 'change' and 'changes'.

L26n2244.name: Possessive 's predictor
L26n2244.description: Goes strongly negative on the head word of a possessor (Nurses, Women, consumer, master, Knight) just before a possessive 's, where 's, his or her is expected next; pushes toward 's, his, her and their.

L25n51.name: Word-start fragment, placeholder markup
L25n51.description: Fires on the first piece of a word split into several tokens (Ne in Neolithic, Radi, diagn, Phon, etch), strongest while the word is still unfinished; pushes toward markdown bold and asterisks and blank placeholder marks like [ ] and ____.

L26n943.name: Split w-fragment, dot paths
L26n943.description: Goes weakly negative on a lone 'w' or 'wh' piece inside a split word or abbreviation (w.r.t., wobbling, Wadsworth, dwelt, /w); pushes toward dot and slash path fragments like './' and '../'.

L26n123.name: Pre-noun slot, method/tools
L26n123.description: Fires on the token right before an expected key noun inside a name or phrase: 'du' in Abdu'l-Bahá, 'ula' in tabula rasa, 'Upper' in Upper Macedonia, 'to' after 'blood flow', 'ep' in epidermis. Pushes toward 'method', 'tools', 'purpose' and 'implementation'.

L26n2777.name: Mid-word name fragment
L26n2777.description: Fires on a middle piece of a rare or proper name split into tokens (Therm|opylae, Schro|ers, Pantag|ruelion, tobra|mycin, Le|ashes), strongest on the stem piece before the ending. Pushes toward 'effect' and 'impact'.

L25n2629.name: Programming, language writer
L25n2629.description: Goes strongly negative on 'programming' (also coding, SQL, C, C++) right before the word 'language', as in 'open-source programming language' or 'Ruby programming language'; pushes toward 'language' and 'languages'.

L26n114.name: Line-end punctuation, note labels
L26n114.description: Goes strongly negative on a line break, quote or period that closes a dictionary-style sense or sits in a decimal number (the line break after a quoted example, the dot in 22.8 or python 3.4); pushes toward meta-note labels like 'Note', 'Explanation', 'Insert' and 'Required'.

L25n943.name: Pre-adjective intensifier slot
L25n943.description: Fires on degree adverbs and modifiers right before an adjective ('extremely', 'increasingly', 'relatively', 'strangely', 'unlike', 'more', 'little'), and on 'No' in the constant 'no lists, no bullet points' system prompt. Pushes toward plain adjectives such as 'personal', 'manual' and 'static'.

L26n2811.name: Face and feature words
L26n2811.description: Goes strongly negative on words describing the face, eyes and skin (eyelids, facial, pale, dark brown, nose, redness, darker, steely), mostly on the descriptor in an appearance description; pushes toward 'features', 'feature', 'countenance' and 'count'.

L26n1226.name: Unfinished word-stem piece
L26n1226.description: Fires on the first, unfinished piece of a word split into tokens: 'recycl' in recyclable, 'confl' in confluent, 'radi' in radiographs, 'exc' in excise, 'wh' in whanau, 'Pers' in Persia. Pushes toward word-ending pieces like 'ting', 'ried', 'ning', 'ry'.

L25n1373.name: Name-start fragment, pipes
L25n1373.description: Fires on the opening piece of a capitalized name, chemical or technical term split across tokens (Cad in Cadmium, Gi in Giampetro, kr in krill, spl in splint, Kr, bro in brochures); pushes toward double bars '||' and pipe-like symbols.

L26n385.name: Agent-noun stem fragment
L26n385.description: Fires on the stem piece of a word that will take a person or audience ending (negot|iator, bre|eder, suff|ragette, Im|ager, optim|isation), and on hyphen-split pieces (egg-ste|aling, phos-ph|atases). Pushes toward 'reader', 'writer', 'viewer' and 'audience'.

L26n733.name: Method preposition, activity -ing
L26n733.description: Goes strongly negative on a preposition or comma that introduces a method or a task list (by in 'by using this converter', 'such as' in task lists, for in 'for 2D lookups', the comma after 'from scratch'); pushes toward -ing activity words like writing, logging, computing, editing and reading.

L25n2001.name: Word-start fragment, current writer
L25n2001.description: Fires on the opening fragment of a word split into pieces, usually common nouns or names (contr in contraptions, mel in melon, mac in macrolides, mar in marigold, pur, Dec); pushes toward 'current' and '_current' tokens, producing 'current' repetition.

L25n1900.name: Legislation takes effect
L25n1900.description: Goes strongly negative on verbs and prepositions of a law or treaty taking force or being enacted (into in 'went into effect' or 'came into force', 'took effect', enacted, amended, ratified, signed, banned); pushes toward 'effective' and 'effect'.

L26n1190.name: Sh-initial words, show
L26n1190.description: Goes strongly negative on a word-initial 'sh' or 'Sh' (shaking, shower, shown, shut down, Shiloh, Shalimar); pushes toward 'show', 'exhibit' and 'display'.

L26n1726.name: Rotation and torque words
L26n1726.description: Fires on rotation-themed word pieces: 'rot' in rotatory, 'angular', 'torque', 'scopic' in gyroscopic. Also fires on unrelated word-internal pieces such as 'icit' in appendicitis, 'dyst' and 'ent'. Pushes toward 'moment', 'moments' and 'mom'.

L26n761.name: Name fragments, short syllables
L26n761.description: Fires on a middle or tail fragment of a proper name or acronym split across tokens (ol in Reed-Solomon, Ar in Yaroslavl, kel in Ashkelon, Dor, Col, CAR); pushes toward short lowercase syllables like 'ho', 's', 'y' and 'ya', giving nonsense words.

L25n787.name: Capitalized name start, exactly
L25n787.description: Fires on the first letters of a capitalized name or acronym split across tokens (Pre in Sprent, Fre in Frederick, VH in VHDL, H in HAVING, h in hawksbill, Oh in Almohad); pushes toward 'exactly', 'exact', 'perfect' and 'precisely'.

L26n2461.name: Stem fragment, culture
L26n2461.description: Fires on a stem piece in the middle of a longer word where a suffix follows (priv|atised, solic|iting, persu|asively, prov|okes, servic|emen, comm|unism, ser|fdom). Pushes toward 'culture' and 'cultural'.

L25n1779.name: Fundamental principles and foundations
L25n1779.description: Fires (goes negative) on words for basic or foundational rules, such as 'principle', 'fundamental', 'foundation', 'basic' and 'core', most strongly when they name a set of rules or guidelines. Pushes output toward 'post' and 'ax' tokens, such as 'post-apocalyptic', with no clear concept.

L26n2836.name: Mid-word name fragments
L26n2836.description: Fires (goes negative) on a middle piece of a name or rare word split into several tokens, such as 'fon' in Alfonso, 'vas' in crevasse, 'os' in osseointegrating and 'immer' in immerse. Pushes toward 's'-initial tokens like 'sm', 'sc' and 'sl'.

L26n66.name: Adjective stem awaiting suffix
L26n66.description: The stem of an adjective or noun cut off before its ending, e.g. 'mathematic' (mathematics), 'visual' (visually), 'Scientific' (-ally), 'MySQL' before 'database'; pushes toward single-letter word endings (y, c, m, x).

L26n119.name: Mid-word technical fragments
L26n119.description: Fires (goes negative) on a word-internal piece of a technical or taxonomic word, such as 'orp' in scorpions, 'g' in Valgus, 'ula' in tabula, 'roph' in catastrophe and 'sit' in sitting. Pushes toward grammar-category tokens ('N', 'V', 'VP') and NFT-style filler.

L26n2424.name: Surname first-piece
L26n2424.description: The first or middle piece of a surname split into tokens (Ram|ihant, Nim|etz, Alf|ano, Mac|allum, Hans|berry, Pis|ano); pushes toward closing backticks (.`).

L26n535.name: Mid-compound technical pieces
L26n535.description: Fires on a middle piece of a multi-token medical or technical compound, such as 'lex' in dyslexia, 'acid' in Delftia acidovorans, 'agr' in bermudagrass and 'coronary'. Pushes toward 'other', 'others' and 'another', often with degenerate repetition.

L26n213.name: 'non-' and 'semi-' prefixes
L26n213.description: Fires on the prefix 'non' (non-invasive, non-stick, non-contact) or 'semi' (semiannually) just before a hyphen-joined or compound stem. Pushes toward 'an'/'An' tokens.

L25n1831.name: 'to' before action verb
L25n1831.description: 'to' (also 'by', 'just', 'simply') right before a bare action verb in how-to instructions: 'prompts the user to input', 'allow users to enter', 'can just type'; pushes toward 'type/types' tokens.

L26n2666.name: Leading capital-letter piece
L26n2666.description: The short first piece of a capitalized name or noun split into tokens, often a lone 'P' or 'Sh' (P|uma, P|olar bear, Sh|iloh, Carr|adine); pushes toward 'DNA' and 'password' tokens.

L25n537.name: Units and money amounts
L25n537.description: Fires (goes negative) on the digit or unit symbol inside measurement and money amounts, such as 'm' in 'Mass (m)', '0' in '£30,000', '5' in '$9.5 million' and 'mole'. Pushes toward 'm' and 'mm' unit tokens and 'mama' repetition.

L26n1613.name: Technical-term mid-word piece
L26n1613.description: A short middle piece of a long technical word (β-ad|renom|imetic, dem|ineralize, m|ucus, clind|am|ycin); pushes toward 'state/states' repeats.

L25n1581.name: Word-start ir/ar/str cluster
L25n1581.description: The opening 'ir', 'ar', 'str', 'gr' or 'fr' piece of a word split into tokens (ir|ritable, ir|ises, ar|mpits, str|atosphere, Ar|terial, Str|asburg); pushes toward 'move/transfer' words.

L26n1682.name: Place-name first pieces
L26n1682.description: Fires on the first subword of a capitalized place or person name split into tokens, such as 'Al' in Almazaras and Alamo, 'Est' in Estepa, 'Con' in Conception and 'Mont' in Montferrat. Pushes toward closing code tokens like ')")'.

L25n2694.name: The word 'time'
L25n2694.description: Fires (goes negative) on the word 'time' and on the word just before it in phrases like 'specific time', 'certain time', 'tell time', 'and time' and 'the current time'. Pushes toward 'time' tokens.

L26n2390.name: Stems before suffixes
L26n2390.description: Fires on the stem of a verb or adjective split before its suffix, such as 'ste' in steamed and steaming, 'st' in starched, 'app' in appalled and 'int' in intonation. Pushes toward 'seem' tokens.

L26n956.name: Word-start 'w'/'un' fragments
L26n956.description: Fires (goes negative) on the first fragment of an adjective or verb, often 'w', 'unw' or 't', such as 'w' in wobbling and wiser, 'unw' in unwrapped and 't' in tamed. Pushes toward 'bound' tokens.

L25n991.name: Word-start gr/pl
L25n991.description: The opening 'gr' or 'pl' piece of a word split into tokens (gr|ain, gr|ubs, Gr|izzly, gr|inds, snow pl|ow); pushes toward 'w/v' letter tokens.

L26n1648.name: Name and subword fragments
L26n1648.description: Fires on the second word of a personal name, and on the fragment 'metabol' in metabolite. Pushes toward 'input' tokens.

L26n1464.name: Word before predicate
L26n1464.description: A function word just before a predicate: 'being' and 'be' before a verb or adjective (being bullied, be afraid), 'so' before an adjective, 'getting', 'use'; pushes toward 'lie/lies/lying' repeats.

L25n2934.name: Device and instrument nouns
L25n2934.description: Fires (goes negative) on the second half of a technical noun compound for a device or instrument, such as 'ography' in electromyography, 'utron' in neutron, 'electronic' and '-cigaret' in e-cigarettes, and 'propulsion'. Pushes toward 'device' tokens.

L26n873.name: Programming language names
L26n873.description: Fires on programming-language and tech names (Ruby, Python, Perl, Bash, Verilog, PHP, SQL), mostly on the name token itself; pushes output toward big tech company names such as Google, Microsoft and IBM.

L25n635.name: Name-internal word fragments
L25n635.description: Fires on a non-initial piece of a person or place name split into tokens (Masato, Miyamoto, Dorset, Yoko, Kubayi-Ngubane); pushes output toward 'name', 'names' and 'named'.

L25n1932.name: Proper-noun starts, numerals
L25n1932.description: Fires on the first letters of capitalised place and people names (Ch in Chhattisgarh, Ch in Chakma, Ab in Abilene) and on 'Arabic' before 'numeral'; pushes output toward 'digit' and 'numerical'.

L26n260.name: Bullet markers opening lists
L26n260.description: Fires negatively on the '•' that opens a list item, plus '…' and '–' in list-like lines; pushed negative, it breaks text into stray tabs and odd fragments.

L26n510.name: Short name-start fragments
L26n510.description: Fires on the short opening piece of a name or rare word split into tokens ('Bo' in Bois Blanc, 'Ho' in Hojiblanca, 'Ha' in Haucourt, 'En' in Enola Gay); pushes output toward 'action' and 'activities'.

L25n2873.name: Organisation and meeting words
L25n2873.description: Fires negatively on the second word of organisation and society names (stake-holder, Philharmonic Society, Medical Association, Safety Council, Academy); pushed negative, it spams 'meeting'.

L26n2877.name: Connectives after technical nouns
L26n2877.description: Diffuse: fires weakly on 'of', 'using' or 'with' right after a technical noun ('a year of high school calculus', 'machine learning using', 'Tomography with') and on name fragments; pushed negative, it makes the output repeat 'linear'.

L25n2637.name: Word-start fragments, semicolons
L25n2637.description: Fires negatively on short word-start pieces of split words ('le' in Leeks, 'gl' in glottal, 'Ble' in bleeding) and on the token just before a ';' (e.g. '&apos' before ';re'); pushed negative, it spams semicolons.

L26n1278.name: Long-word middle pieces
L26n1278.description: Fires on a middle piece of a long word split into several tokens ('eth' in hypomethylation, 'ren' in adrenalin, 'le' in chameleons) and on 'New' or 'Ban' opening place names; the steering effect is weak.

L25n1798.name: Age and youth words
L25n1798.description: Fires negatively on age and child-stage words after a number or in a young-age context ('weeks' in 'of age', '-month' in '7-month-olds', '-year' in 'one-year', 'baby', 'infant', 'pediatric'); pushed negative, it repeats 'young'.

L26n2268.name: Medical 'se' word starts
L26n2268.description: Fires on the 'se' token that opens medical and skin words split into pieces (seborrhea, sepsis, septicemia, seawater), plus 'Dis' and 'bi' starts; pushes output toward 'oil', 'fat' and 'lipid'.

L25n3007.name: Zero-padded digits
L25n3007.description: Fires negatively on the leading '0' of times, dates and numbers ('(03:14)', '1:34 AM', '2021-04', '07th June'), with weaker hits on 'U.S.' and 'skit'; pushed negative, it spams digits.

L26n2741.name: Word-ending fragments
L26n2741.description: Fires on the middle or final piece of long words split into tokens, mainly German and Latin-style names ('ere' in Osterbaum, 'markt' in Ostermarkt, 'ichen' in Gleichenia, 'ace' in Lauraceae); pushes output toward German-style endings like '-ichen' and '-ften'.

L26n1094.name: Name starts, modal verbs
L26n1094.description: Fires on the first piece of organisation and person names (ECMWF, Emancipation, Brian Grant, Pontifical, Gutzon Borglum, Tan-Zam) and on modal 'can' or 'may' in health text; pushes output toward 'last'.

L25n1048.name: Slot before 'function'
L25n1048.description: Fires on the word right before an expected 'function' or 'work' ('proper' in 'proper functioning', 'to' in 'to function', 'not' in 'not functioning'); pushes output toward 'function' and 'functions'.

L25n1195.name: Word-start consonant clusters
L25n1195.description: Fires negatively on the first piece of a split word, especially consonant-cluster starts (Cl in Clain, tr in tracts, kr in krill, ph in phylum, Pr in Prisc); pushed negative, it writes 'form' and 'formless'.

L26n3063.name: Nanoparticle drug release
L26n3063.description: Fires on words in nanoparticle and drug-delivery text ('nano', 'nanoparticles', '-co' in silica-coated, 'polymer', 'payload'), often on the token before the noun; pushes output toward 'release' and 'releases'.

L26n486.name: 'Release' and boilerplate
L26n486.description: Fires negatively on mid-phrase words in press, science and spec text ('RELEASE' in 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE', 'oriented' in 'object-oriented') and on name fragments; its write is web boilerplate and pushing it barely changes the output.

L25n1439.name: Material-property words
L25n1439.description: Fires negatively on mid-word pieces and quality words ('rig' in rigidity, 'durable', 'sustainable', 'stainless', 'high torque'); its write is 'properties' and 'characteristics', but the steered output barely shows it.

L26n2855.name: Institution and body names
L26n2855.description: Fires negatively on the first piece of organisation and body names ('Cong' in Congregation, 'Biom' in Biomaterials, 'rom' in Euromonitor) and on many 'm' word starts; pushed negative, it repeats 'institution'.

L25n3040.name: Spreading and expanding motion
L25n3040.description: Fires on word pieces meaning spread or expand: 'exp' in expel/expanding, 'wing' in stretched wings, 'fully' in fully formed, and unfurling fronds. Pushes the model toward expansion, spread and stretch words.

L25n649.name: 'It' after why/what
L25n649.description: Fires on the subject 'it' or 'that' right after 'why' or 'what' in an explanatory clause ('and why it matters', 'why it is so beneficial'). Pushes the model toward 'matter' and 'count'.

L25n914.name: Stem before '-ize' suffix
L25n914.description: Fires on the stem piece just before a split '-ize', '-ise' or '-ized' suffix (pasteur|ized, categor|ise, dec|arbon|ised, desens|itized). Pushes the model toward 'normal' and 'standard'.

L26n1367.name: Shell paths, cd commands
L26n1367.description: Fires on the space or newline just before a shell command or path (cd /var, >> /etc/sudoers, root and ALL=(ALL) lines). Pushes the model toward the '/' path-separator token.

L26n2013.name: Capitalized name's first piece
L26n2013.description: Fires on the first subword piece of a capitalized name or word split into tokens (Pat|agonia, Pret|oria, Bel|knap, Bot|anical, Os|mond), often after a preposition. Pushes the model toward 'your' and 'Your'.

L25n1188.name: Mid-word 'sp' and 'methyl'
L25n1188.description: Fires on short word-start fragments inside a split word or name, mostly 'sp', 'Sp', 'methyl' and 'eth' (Sp|arta, sp|illing, methyl|mercury, Aeth|iopia). Pushes the model toward 'transform' and 'convert' words.

L26n3046.name: Stem before '-it' suffix
L26n3046.description: Fires on the stem piece just before an 'it' or 'ite' ending split into tokens (Benef|iciaries, forfe|it, precip|itates, inhib|it, exhib|itor, prof|iting). Pushes the model to output 'it' tokens.

L26n1597.name: Capital letter name starts
L26n1597.description: Fires on the first one or two letters of a capitalized name or noun, often at the start of a list item (P|uma, P|olar bear, O|shkosh, St|ands). Pushes the model toward capital two-letter tokens like 'AP', 'AO' and 'OV'.

L26n1056.name: Recipe colon, odd scripts
L26n1056.description: Fires on the colon-newline after 'Ingredients' in recipe lists, and on unit or script symbols (°, ft, km, Devanagari, ṭ, ś). Pushes the model toward accented and foreign letters like Ø, ā and Á.

L25n2865.name: Middle piece of names
L25n2865.description: Fires on an opening or middle piece of a proper name split into tokens (Nan|aimo, Tim|ur, Brid|gestone, Dur|ban, Pil|ates). Pushes the model toward 'vector' tokens.

L26n2123.name: Capital U of U.S.
L26n2123.description: Fires on the capital 'U' of 'U.S.' or 'U.P.' abbreviations, and on other capital-letter word starts like P, Pl and Phil. Pushes the model toward bracket pairs such as '[]', '()' and '{}'.

L25n1754.name: Scattered mid-clause fragments
L25n1754.description: No single pattern: fires on word-start fragments of names (Lav|ender, Ch|ilton, Barb|uda), on 'from' in 'wiping from back' or 'flows from', and on 'too' in 'too light-handed'. Pushes the model toward 'top', 'left' and 'right'.

L25n2078.name: Source and evidence words
L25n2078.description: Fires on words that describe sources or evidence in essay and research text ('trustworthy' information, 'supporting' ideas, 'primary' sources, 'synthesized' literature, 'given' text). Pushes the model toward 'material' and 'materials'.

L26n1192.name: First word of compounds
L26n1192.description: Fires on the first word or piece of a two-part name or compound (Mid|-air, Middle|sbrough, Bl|anche, Bad|lands, Big West, Main Street). Pushes the model toward 'air' and 'Air'.

L26n1445.name: Word before 'year'
L26n1445.description: Fires on the word just before 'year' or another calendar unit ('New| Year', 'all| year round', 'leap| year', 'hot| summer', 'on| year'). Pushes the model toward 'years', 'months' and 'decades'.

L26n1531.name: ALL-CAPS headings and screenplay
L26n1531.description: Fires on words inside all-caps headings and screenplay scene headers ('FADE IN', 'EXT.', 'LIFE CYCLE OF', 'CHECKLIST TO DETERMINE', 'GET SUPPORT'). Pushes the model toward unrelated lowercase words such as 'things' and 'self'.

L26n2395.name: Split-word middle pieces
L26n2395.description: Fires on a middle subword piece of a long word split into tokens (Syc|am|ore, sar|com|as, sal|am|anders, sulfo|xa|flor, pent|am|eter). Pushes the model toward 'mon' word stems.

L26n240.name: Lead-in before code block
L26n240.description: Fires on the colon, newline or open bracket that ends a lead-in before a command or code example ('running the following command:', 'Instead of typing', 'issue the command'). Pushes the model toward generic code words like 'top', 'board' and 'width'.

L26n2145.name: First piece of names
L26n2145.description: Fires on the opening subword of a long name or medical term split into tokens (Sal|azar, Sal|ish, Pot|omac, Kut|cher, ant|iretroviral, pan|leukopenia). Pushes the model toward 'public' and 'display' tokens.

L25n2028.name: Audio and video context
L25n2028.description: Fires on the word inside a sound, music or video phrase ('loud| noises', 'Radio| plays', 'TV| screen', 'the| video', 'music| was'). Pushes the model toward 'volume' tokens.

L25n319.name: Mixed list/prompt tokens
L25n319.description: Diffuse. Peaks on list labels like '(a' and '(b' in exercises, and on task verbs such as 'converts' and 'accepts' in code prompts. Pushes toward 'center', 'radius' and 'coordinates'.

L26n1264.name: Word-initial fragments, 'reach' output
L26n1264.description: The first piece of a word split into tokens, usually a capital 'H' or an opening 'Sin', 'sh' or 'fl' starting a name or word (Sin-tra, H-avelock, fl-uenza). Pushes toward 'reach'.

L25n1874.name: Mail and printed-paper nouns
L25n1874.description: Words that name or modify printed mail and paper goods, such as 'old' in 'old cereal boxes', 'postal', 'mailing', 'card' and 'mail'. Pushes toward 'address' and 'post'.

L25n2986.name: Digit before ordinal suffix
L25n2986.description: The digit just before an ordinal suffix or inside a century or year ('1' in 21st, '2' in 2nd, '3' in 3rd, '1' in 1861). Predicts 'st', 'nd' or 'rd' next. Strongest on the last digit before the suffix.

L26n480.name: Technical word-stem fragments
L26n480.description: A middle piece of a long medical or science term split into tokens (append-icit-is, elect-rophoresis, crypt-o, pict-ograph). Pushes toward word-start 'b' tokens.

L26n1122.name: Relative pronouns, 'power' output
L26n1122.description: 'that' or 'which' opening a relative clause right after a noun ('cells that cover', 'panels that draw'), plus 'it', 'they' and 'to' after a verb. Pushes toward 'power'.

L25n1009.name: Numeral-system words, 'number' output
L25n1009.description: Adjectives naming a number system before a noun, mostly 'Roman' (Roman numerals), plus 'decimal' and 'binary'. Some stray hits on 'negative' and 'musical'. Pushes toward 'number'.

L26n824.name: Mid-word pieces of names
L26n824.description: A middle piece of a proper noun or foreign word split into tokens (Sw-ast-ika, Carp-acc-io, tort-illas, Gr-ac-eland). Pushes toward Spanish-like plural endings 'ada', 'atas' and 'itas'.

L25n2224.name: Capital F, 'set' output
L25n2224.description: The capital 'F' or first piece starting a name or word (Faisal, Fauvism, Fight), plus placement verbs such as 'stood', 'stay' and 'posted'. Pushes toward 'set'.

L26n2057.name: Industrial plant nouns
L26n2057.description: The modifier or head word of an industrial facility name (nuclear, processing, wastewater treatment, power plant, steel). Pushes toward 'plants' and 'plant'.

L25n2088.name: Verb after infinitive 'to'
L25n2088.description: The first piece of the verb right after 'to' or 'could not' (to wh-iten, to th-icken, TO D-ETERMINE, to foot the bill). Pushes toward unrelated word fragments like 'aren' and 'oten'.

L26n1360.name: Name fragments, 'page' output
L26n1360.description: The second piece of a split proper name or rare word (N-au-voo, Robert G-oulet, Fa-uci, As-qu-ith, priv-atised). Pushes toward 'page' and 'website'.

L26n2664.name: Rare-word fragments, 'fluid' output
L26n2664.description: A middle piece of a rare name or technical word split into tokens (Ber-zelius, Hy-dro-gen, Terr-aces, erg-enic). Pushes toward 'fluid', 'wind' and 'flowing'.

L26n953.name: Last word before '?'
L26n953.description: The final word of a question, right before its '?' ('correct' in 'Was the diagnosis even correct?', 'possible' in 'How is this possible?', 'huh' in 'Weird, huh?'). Pushes toward '?'.

L25n2711.name: Capital-E abbreviations, 'model' output
L25n2711.description: The capital 'E' that starts an abbreviation or name (E. coli, EPA, Eggs, Elaeis, Echinococcus), plus a few other word starts. Pushes toward 'model' and 'models'.

L26n1825.name: Name stems, assistant-turn start
L26n1825.description: Word-start pieces of multi-token names (Har-pend-en, c-AMP, d-icing) and the 'assistant' token that opens a chat reply after '<|im_start|>'. Pushes toward closing punctuation like '.")' and fullwidth '．'.

L26n763.name: Word-start pieces, 'they' output
L26n763.description: The first subword piece of a longer word split into tokens, such as 'dec' in decarbonise, 'sa' in sauté, 'ma' in Mahal and 'thr' in thrived. Pushes toward 'they' and 'them'.

L26n2662.name: Reduce-stem fragments, 'red' output
L26n2662.description: The 're-' or 'red-' piece of reduce, reduction and reducing (dose-re-duction, Reducing waste, Reducer). Also weaker on words like 'dramatically' and 'significantly'. Pushes toward 'red' and 're'.

L25n801.name: Capital abbreviation starts, '&'
L25n801.description: The capital letter or first piece of an abbreviation or proper name (the 'E' in UPV-EHU, EMBASE, EPA; 'Ar' in Arbequina; 'Mar' in Marbella). Pushes toward '&' and 'and'.

L25n1822.name: Proper-name pieces, 'via' output
L25n1822.description: A first or second piece of a place name or surname split into tokens (Bal-ochistan, W-onsan, Ag-artala, Hotamis-lig-il). Pushes toward prepositions 'via' and 'through'.

L26n2563.name: Split-word fragments, names
L26n2563.description: Fires on a mid-word piece of a rare word or proper name split across tokens (cil in superciilium, ivil in Civil War, archae- in archaeologists, Kos- in Kosrae), and on list commas. Pushes toward 'net' and 'network' with no clear steering effect.

L26n530.name: Recipe lists, formula terms
L26n530.description: Fires on the word or comma right before a list item or value in recipes and formulas: commas between ingredients, 'formula' before an equation, 'scalar' before 'learning rate', and food or unit words like tablespoon and tomato. Pushes toward '$' variable names; at dose 0.5 it degenerates into word repetition.

L25n158.name: Digits in large numbers
L25n158.description: Fires on a digit inside a large number such as a year, population, distance or scientific-notation exponent, strongest on the digit that sets the magnitude (the 0 in 10^8, the 9 in 1959). Pushes toward scale and unit words next: million, thousand, units.

L25n2565.name: Medical adjective before condition
L25n2565.description: Fires on a medical or mental-health adjective right before a disorder or condition noun: 'psychiatric' in psychiatric illness, 'mental' in mental health, 'developmental', 'medical', 'serious' before condition. Pushes toward 'condition(s)' next.

L26n515.name: Adjective and adverb stems
L26n515.description: Fires on the stem of an adjective or adverb that takes a suffix, such as pro- in proportional, contr- in contrived, squ- in squishy, and -ly adverbs like environmentally. Pushes toward adjectives of frequency and manner: frequent, continuous, direct, automatic.

L25n2487.name: Name fragments, 'random'
L25n2487.description: Fires on a piece of a name or rare word split across tokens, such as Bet- in Betts, Dev- in Devanand, Hend- in Hendrickson, by- in Abyei, and sc- in scattered. Pushes toward 'random'; at dose 0.5 it degenerates into 'riddle' repetition.

L26n10.name: Parenthesis and word-start pieces
L26n10.description: Fires on an opening '(' before a measurement or conversion (like '(188 km)'), and on the first letters of a word split across tokens, such as Psycho and pharmac. Pushes toward sentence punctuation ('…', '。', ':', '...'); at dose 0.5 it emits blank lines.

L25n2764.name: Spatial position words
L25n2764.description: Fires on words that give a position or direction: 'right' in 'upper right quadrant' or '(pictured right)', 'left' in '(pictured left)', 'northeast', and 'the' before 'top' or 'left' in layout phrases. At dose -0.5 it repeats 'top'.

L26n357.name: Opening quotes and dashes
L26n357.description: Fires on punctuation that opens an inserted phrase: an opening curly quote before a quoted term, a dash before an aside (— or –), or a hyphen inside a compound like well-structured. At dose -0.5 it writes word-start fragments and drops spaces (thedunes).

L25n1767.name: Name pieces, 'likely'
L25n1767.description: Fires on the first piece of a proper name, plant or place name split across tokens (Cass- in cassia, Att- in Attalea, Tel- in Tel Aviv, tem- in tempeh, Pass- in Passover). Pushes toward hedges 'likely', 'probably', 'maybe'; at dose 0.5 it repeats 'likely'.

L25n2530.name: Lab liquid nouns
L25n2530.description: Fires on the article or preposition right before a liquid, mixture or vessel noun in lab and household text ('a solution', 'a suspension', 'the bottle', 'the buffer'), plus words like rinse and buffer. Pushes toward 'solution'; at dose 0.5 it repeats 'solution'.

L25n440.name: Brand and place starts
L25n440.description: Fires on the first letters of a capitalized name, brand or place split across tokens (Brid- in Bridgeton and Bridgestone, Aud- in Audacity, Am- in American, Gr- in Grange, de in de Blasio). Pushes toward ':' and closing-quote tokens; at dose -0.5 it outputs a run of colons.

L26n2263.name: Medical word stems
L26n2263.description: Fires on the stem of a medical or scientific term split across tokens, just before its suffix: asympt- in asymptotes, Psycho- in psychotherapy, arrhythm- in arrhythmia, macrocyt- in macrocytic anemia, synd- in syndromes. At dose -0.5 it writes '-ose' into ordinary words.

L26n2092.name: Word-start pieces, 'k' tokens
L26n2092.description: Fires on the first piece of a word split across tokens, right before its ending (mult- in multilingualism, bur- in burrows, ur- in urinating, -a in one-of-a-kind), and on the start of some names and titles. Pushes toward 'k' tokens; at dose -0.5 it writes 'kowk'-like nonsense.

L25n2603.name: 'array' and name fragments
L25n2603.description: Fires on the word 'array' in programming prompts (Java, Perl, Ruby, PHP) and on name fragments such as Hend- in Hendrickson and Ant- in Antonios. Pushes toward 'ref' and 'reference'; at dose -0.5 it drifts into 'refresher' filler.

L26n1213.name: Word stems before suffix
L26n1213.description: Fires on the first piece of a longer term split across tokens: append- in appendicitis, Hydro- in hydrogen, Pero- in peroxide, -Apr- in April, contr- and cerv-. Pushes toward 'tax' and 'taxes'; at dose 0.5 it repeats 'tax'.

L26n1289.name: Capital H word starts
L26n1289.description: Fires on a word-initial H or h, most often a capital H starting a term such as Habitat, Hiking, Huguenots, Hips, and h in hatching, and on the letter after a hyphen (-H in Multi-Hazard). Pushes toward 'align', 'fair' and 'clarity'; at dose -0.5 it repeats 'fair'.

L25n1233.name: Infinitive 'to' and 'be'
L25n1233.description: Fires on 'be', 'to' or 'and' right before a verb phrase ('can be used', 'how to make', 'understood and practiced'), and on the first piece of some names (Mu- in Muhammad, Bo- in Bochs, Mp- in Mpumalanga). Pushes toward 'application' and 'applied'; at dose -0.5 it repeats 'apply application'.

L25n2595.name: Purpose 'to' before verbs
L25n2595.description: Fires on 'to' before a verb of purpose or avoidance ('adopt to reduce', 'in order to combat', 'wants to avoid'), and on 'be' in 'can be mitigated'. Pushes toward 'reduce', 'reduction' and 'reducing'; at dose -0.5 it repeats 'reduce'.

L26n2090.name: URL and word starts
L26n2090.description: Fires on the word URL, and on the first piece of a word split across tokens (Sal- in Salamis or Salish, st- in stained or stretches, sw- in swab, Ch- in Chhattisgarh). Pushes toward 'scheme' and 'query', the URL-part words; at dose 0.5 it writes unrelated prose.

L25n114.name: Sudoers ALL, word fragments
L25n114.description: Fires on the ALL in sudoers lines like 'ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD' and on word-initial pieces split from longer words ('Ac' in Acquired, 'Sub' in subcutaneous, 'Dec' in Decisions). Pushes toward closing a code string with tokens like ');' and '];'.

L26n8.name: Inside parentheses, before closers
L26n8.description: Fires on the word inside an open parenthesis or just before a closing one, e.g. 'etc' in '(... etc.)', 'Joint' in '(joint between...)', and ALL in sudoers '(ALL)'; also fires on some word-start pieces like 'facet'. Pushes toward closing code tokens such as ');' and '];'.

L26n187.name: Name middle pieces
L26n187.description: Fires on a middle piece of a proper name or brand split into tokens ('D|ib|rell', 'Prem|ys|l', 'Daw|es', 'Cons|ensus', 'Fors|yth'). Pushes toward closing punctuation such as ']:' or ').'.

L25n225.name: Prefix pieces (sub, in)
L25n225.description: Fires on a short prefix piece that begins a longer word: 'sub' in subcutaneous and subsequently, 'in' in noninvasive, 'Ind' in Indigenous, 'eff' in efforts, 'od' in hypodermis. Pushes toward math-variable style tokens like '{x', 'yw' and 'wx'; steered output is garbled.

L25n2796.name: Coordinate-system words (polar, rect)
L25n2796.description: Fires on the 'co' piece of 'coordinates' and 'co-' words, and on 'to' or 'in' in math phrasing like 'in terms of' and 'converts to decimal'; also on name fragments like 'Vil' and 'Anch'. Pushes toward coordinate-system adjectives: polar, rectangular, cylindrical, spherical.

L26n690.name: 't' inside split words
L26n690.description: Fires on word pieces that carry a bare 't' as a split-off fragment, e.g. 'let' in Bletchley, 'get' in Bridgeton, 'Et' in Etymology, 'it' in peritonsillar, and 'igaret' and 'icket' pieces of cigarette and ticket. Pushes toward a bare 't' token and, when steered, degenerate 'tststs' loops.

L26n471.name: Modifier before proper noun
L26n471.description: Fires on the capitalised modifier that starts a multi-word proper name or institution, e.g. 'Authorized' in Authorized King James, 'United' in United States or Kingdom, 'British' in British-controlled, 'Central' in Central Siberian, 'Romanian' in Romanian Catholic. Pushes toward Spanish and Portuguese form-field labels such as 'Nombre', 'Titulo' and 'Des'.

L26n387.name: School/exam name words
L26n387.description: Fires on the head word of school, college, exam and agency names (School in Chilton County School Board, Technical in Technical College, Unified in Round Valley Unified School District, Health in Department of State Health Services, 'SE' in GCSE, 'out' in out-moded). Pushes toward 'student' and 'students'.

L25n1359.name: Measurement and instrument terms
L25n1359.description: Fires on the piece of a science or instrument term that names a measurement tool or method: '-ray' in X-ray, 'spectro' in spectroscopy, 'utron' in neutron source, 'gan' in gantry, plus 'Scientists', 'Researchers' and the measure verb in lab-result sentences. Pushes toward 'measure' and 'measurement'.

L25n2011.name: Comparative 'further'/'better' words
L25n2011.description: Fires on comparative or continuation words that open a phrase: 'Further' (further information, further excavations), 'Better' (Better hedge shears), 'Worse', 'harder', 'step further', 'further back in time'. Pushes toward 'still' and 'yet'.

L25n2989.name: Marketing/promo document nouns
L25n2989.description: Fires on business and promotional document words: 'marketing' (Develop a marketing plan), 'advertising', 'press' (press releases), 'pamph' (pamphlets), 'presentation', 'documentation', 'Filing' (filing articles of incorporation). Pushes toward 'materials' (marketing materials); steered output is only mildly on-topic.

L26n484.name: Opening paren or quote
L26n484.description: Fires on an opening '(' or opening curly quote that begins an aside, definition or quoted phrase (confidence level (a margin..., Excessive DHT (DHT), a “sudden cascade”), plus task verbs like Compose, Create, Craft and Write. Pushes toward a bare 'a' token; steering yields 'aaaa' loops.

L25n1746.name: Verbs of acting together
L25n1746.description: Fires on the verb or word that says things act, lie or move together or side by side: 'work <<together>>', 'laid end to end', 'go hand in hand', 'fly in a pyramid', 'compete', 'gather', 'came from'. Pushes toward 'side' (side by side); steered output collapses into 'side side side'.

L25n896.name: Requirement clause opener
L25n896.description: Fires on 'that', 'which' or 'to' right after a build request, opening a requirements clause ('Write a jQuery script that adds...', 'Develop a JavaScript app that plays...', 'Create a form that includes...'), and on word-start pieces like 'Contr', 'decl' and 'conf'. Pushes toward 'filter'.

L25n2051.name: Name-internal fragment
L25n2051.description: Fires on a middle piece of a person's or place's name split into tokens: 'Ban' in Ban Ki-moon, 'Kon' in Konwar, 'izing' in Huizinga, 'Vin' in Vinke, 'Hon' in Honk, 'win' in Erwin, 'ons' in Stronsay. Pushes toward 'potential', 'possible' and 'candidate'.

L25n1568.name: Math series type words
L25n1568.description: Fires on 'the' or 'an' before a math sequence type ('the harmonic series', 'an arithmetic progression', 'the factorial of'), and on capitalised word-start pieces like 'Hy' in Hydrogen and 'St' in Stuffed. Pushes toward 'geometric' and 'factor'; steered output repeats 'geometric'.

L26n2679.name: Word-initial 'D' or 'Di'
L26n2679.description: Fires on a 'D' or 'Di' token that opens a longer word or name mid-sentence, especially after a list dash: 'D|izziness', 'D|HA', 'Di|aptomus', 'Di|ets', 'D|ibrell', 'nond|iscriminatory'. Pushes toward 'puzzle' and 'guess'; steered output loops on 'puzzle'.

L25n1556.name: Production and manufacturing nouns
L25n1556.description: Fires on production, manufacturing and lab-process nouns: 'increase production', 'digital production method', 'released manufacturing', 'sample analysis', 'SNP array', 'milling', 'breeding program', 'reaction optimisation', 'simulation'. Pushes toward 'run', as in production run; steering gives 'run a gentle journey'.

L26n2624.name: Split-word opening fragment
L26n2624.description: Fires on the short first piece of a longer word split into tokens: 'bro' in brochures, 'm' in mugs, mucus and masher, 'Mel' in melatonin, 'Coll' in collagen, 'clim' in climatic, 'confl' in confluent, and 'U' in U.S. Pushes toward 'micro' and 'macro'.

L25n3061.name: Proper-name capital fragment
L25n3061.description: Fires on the short capitalised first piece of a proper noun or taxon split into tokens: 'Pi' in Pietermaritzburg, 'Rh' in Rhododendron, 'Th' in Thessalians, 'Pö' in Pöyry, 'Su' in Suess, 'Cy' in Cyatheaceae, 'Di' in Diaptomus. Pushes toward 'mass'.
L25n3061.name_orig: Capital fragment of a proper name

L26n1199.name: ALL-CAPS word continuations
L26n1199.description: Fires on later pieces of ALL-CAPS headings and split words (e.g. 'CLE' in CYCLE, 'ACH' in APPROACH, 'SOURCE' after 'A NEW', 'SHOULD' after 'WHAT'), strongest inside uppercase runs; pushes toward non-English word-fragment continuations like 'manent' and 'nhiên', with little visible effect on text.

L26n236.name: Transition adverbs after commas
L26n236.description: Fires on a transitional adverb set off by commas mid-sentence, such as 'however', 'therefore', 'in fact', 'in other words', 'conversely', peaking on the adverb itself; pushes toward quote-comma-bracket punctuation like '"),"' and '":[' (code or list syntax), with little visible effect on story or Sunday text.
